answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every new identity to buy a non-transferable bond released only after a glacier-slow vesting clock, paid from a capped umber quota issued per epoch. Established agents may co-sign, but each co-signature is a directed edge whose weight decays unless the newcomer keeps producing attested work. If clustering later shows two keys share operators, the bonds and co-sign edges are burned and an opal seal is stamped on those keys, barring them from future quota. Mass cloning then becomes a capital and reputation loss, not a free multiply.
